scope: Native long64 CPL0 non-LOCK immediate memory BT/BTS/BTR/BTC for 32- and 64-bit operands. Register-index memory, LOCK, 16-bit and user-mode forms retain interpreter fallback.
motivation: Live production CPU0 profile: __free_pages_core BTR imm13 (480fba300d) was the hottest interpreter-helper fallback, 483801 hits in an observed snapshot.
validation: 122 tests in 4 suites passed. Baseline and optimizing tiers; all four operations; indices 0,13,31,32,63,64,255; zero/all-one values; base and RIP-relative addressing; full state/memory agreement; restartable-read decline, cross-boundary read fault and rejected write rollback; LOCK/register-index/user-mode gates.
limitations: Isolated validation checkout with exact changed sources and current reference interpreter, not all-HEAD qualification.
The first trial used an outdated isolated interpreter before the committed immediate-bit-mask fix; that fixture was corrected before final validation.
No end-to-end boot speed improvement or completed Linux boot claimed.
